content: 1. How did the surveillance system for the event or pathogen evolve during the response? For instance, was there a transition from aggregate reporting to case-based surveillance? 2. What were the specific barriers encountered in implementing effective contact tracing, if applicable? 3. How was the risk associated with the event assessed? Who conducted the assessment, and at what point in time? 4. How were the results of the risk assessment utilized? Did they influence the management of the response? 5. In what ways did the findings from the risk assessment contribute to planning the response efforts? Laboratory 6. What was the laboratory turnaround time? Specifically, how quickly were samples collected, tested, and results reported? 7. What processes were in place for laboratory confirmation of cases? 8. How was the information generated by laboratories managed and disseminated? 9. Were the plans and standard operating procedures for laboratory testing sufficient to address the demands of the event? 10. Were adequate resources—human, material, and financial—available to ensure consistent laboratory support throughout the outbreak? 11. Were there any challenges related to the collection, management, and transportation of specimens? 12. How effective was the coordination and information-sharing between laboratories within the health sector and across other sectors? 13. What role did international reference laboratories play in confirming the event? 14. Were there any accidents or biosafety incidents during laboratory operations? If so, what were the causes? Vector Surveillance and Control 15. What vector control measures were implemented during the emergency, and how did these measures influence the progression of the outbreak? 16. How effectively was the integrated vector management plan executed? 17. How were communities engaged and informed during vector control activities? Did they accept and support the vector control strategies? 18. How was intersectoral coordination and collaboration managed, and how did this contribute to the efficiency of vector control measures? 19. Were sufficient resources available and accessible for vector control activities? 20. Were resistance patterns to the chemical products used for vector control detected? How was resistance monitored and managed? Communication and Community Engagement 21. How were risk communication activities and messages coordinated across different levels of the health system (local, regional, national) and with partner organizations? Did the messages reach the intended target groups, and were they understood? 22. Is there a national risk communication strategy? How was public communication conducted during the emergency? Was a specific communication plan developed? Were there any components of the strategy that proved irrelevant or ineffective? 23. Did the risk assessment inform risk communication efforts, and vice versa? Was there cooperation between personnel responsible for risk communication and those conducting risk assessments? 24. How was risk communication monitored during the emergency? Were there observable changes in public behavior or perceptions as a result of the communication efforts? 25. Did the population most in need of receiving communication messages effectively receive them? If not, why? How was this determined? 26. Were sufficient resources, including budget, available to conduct risk communication and community mobilization? 27. How were communication activities and messages coordinated with other sectors and partners? 28. How were rumors and misinformation identified, and what measures were taken to counter them? 29. How effective was public communication in building trust with the public and addressing emerging concerns? 30. Were mechanisms in place to listen to at-risk communities or allow them to contact authorities with questions? Was feedback from communities used to update risk communication messages and strategies? Evaluation Ratings Definitions 31. Activities performed without challenges (P): The targets and critical tasks associated with the core capability were completed in a manner that achieved the objectives without negatively impacting the performance of other activities. The activity did not contribute to additional health or safety risks for the public or emergency workers and was conducted in accordance with applicable plans, policies, procedures, regulations, and laws. 32. Activities performed with some challenges (S): The targets and critical tasks were completed and achieved the objectives without negatively impacting other activities. However, opportunities to enhance effectiveness and/or efficiency were identified. 33. Activities performed with major challenges (M): The targets and critical tasks were completed, but some or all of the following issues were observed: performance negatively impacted other activities, contributed to additional health or safety risks, or was not conducted in accordance with applicable plans, policies, procedures, regulations, and laws. 34. Activities unable to be performed (U): The targets and critical tasks were not performed in a manner that achieved the objectives. After Action Review (AAR) Report Guidance 35. The AAR report should document and structure discussions during the review, highlighting the analysis and recommendations arising from the review. 36. The report should be shared with team members for their comments before broader circulation for knowledge-sharing purposes. Executive Summary 37. Provide a brief description of the event, a summary of discussions (including notable best practices and challenges), conclusions, and recommendations. Include a timeline of key milestones. Background on Emergency 38. Summarize the key characteristics of the event, including a timeline (e.g., onset date, key milestones, epi curve), how the event was detected via existing systems, a summary of the response, and relevant contextual factors (geographical, political, socioeconomic, environmental). Scope and Objective of Review 39. Describe the rationale for organizing the review, the scope and objectives of the AAR, and the target focus areas. Indicate whether this is a subreport of a larger review or a standalone report. Methods 40. Describe the method and approach used for the review, including the format (e.g., debrief, working group, key informant interviews, mixed-method format), participating organizations, and reference materials used. Findings 41. Detail the discussions covered in the review, structured according to the response pillars reviewed. Highlight root causes, best practices, challenges, and new capacities developed during the response. Key Activities and Recommendations 42. Include all key activities and recommendations identified during the AAR. Next Steps 43. Summarize participants’ discussions on strategies for implementing the activities identified during the AAR. Conclusions 44. Summarize the discussions, key points, and analyses. Include how recommendations will be implemented and tracked, specifying accountability for implementation. Propose any improvements to methodologies for conducting the AAR.
